title: Nepali migrants diverted to Malawi (Blantyre rescue)
summary: According to UNODC, six Nepali nationals said they had been recruited through an agent about a year earlier and set out to reach the United States via Bolivia. Instead they were moved over months through Vietnam, Madagascar, Jordan, Dubai, Azerbaijan and Ethiopia (where they stayed four months), then brought to Malawi and told they would have to work there instead. They were locked in a house in Blantyre with their passports taken. Nepal's Anti-Human Trafficking Bureau, alerted by the families, tipped off Malawian police, who rescued the group on 6 November 2019. The victims were repatriated to Nepal and Malawian police said a Malawian suspect was arrested. UNODC describes them as presumed victims; no court outcome is reported and the agent is not named.
